response.answer:
I cannot confirm a GCNet paper from the supplied material. In the supplied evidence, I do not see any mention of GCNet or a proposed method named GCNet; the evidence items are about `pvigs.pdf`.

The supplied title-page excerpt identifies the document as: “PViGS: Sparse-view 3D Gaussian splatting with pixelwise visibility-aware regularization” by Yixiang Xie, Huabiao Qin, Bin Feng, in *Neurocomputing* [pvigs.pdf, p.1]. The proposed method in that paper is PViGS, described as a visibility-aware 3D Gaussian Splatting approach that introduces pixel-wise visibility attributes from Plane Sweep Volumes into Gaussian radiance fields [pvigs.pdf, p.14], with visibility-guided regularization and PSV-wise semantic regularization [pvigs.pdf, p.14][pvigs.pdf, p.7]. This does not appear to be the GCNet paper you asked about.

Citation note: From the supplied title-page excerpt, I can see authors, title, and the journal *Neurocomputing* [pvigs.pdf, p.1]. The supplied excerpt does not include volume/issue, article number, or publication year, so I cannot provide a complete citation from the supplied evidence.

Limitation: Because no GCNet paper appears in the supplied evidence, I cannot name its proposed method or cite it. If a GCNet paper was intended to be included, it does not appear in the supplied evidence; please provide it and I can extract the method name and citation from that document.

. Conclusion
This paper studies the task of novel view synthesis (NVS) and scene 
representation in sparse-view scenarios. Since 3D Gaussian Splatting 
(3DGS) is prone to overfitting the sparse input images, leading to inaccu­
rate representations such as floaters and incorrect shape. To address this 
challenge, the Visibility-aware 3D Gaussian Splatting approach PViGS is 
proposed, which introduces pixel-wise visibility attributes from Plane 
Sweep Volumes (PSV) into Gaussian radiance fields. Our PViGS effec­
tively enables the explicit modeling of spatial occlusion relationships 
via the new learnable Gaussian parameters. Furthermore, we design 
the visibility-guided regularization strategy and the PSV-wise semantic

3.5 . PSV-wise semantic regularization
Previous semantic regularization methods [ 13,16,74] conduct se­
mantic alignment through optimizing the perceptual distance between 
rendered and training views, facilitating the reconstruction of the global 
structure of the scene. Although traditional semantic regularization ef­
fectively leverages the common semantics across different views as 
smoothness constraints, it is prone to overfitting when facing sparse-
view scenarios. To cope with this challenge, a novel PSV-wise semantic 
regularization strategy is proposed via Plane Sweep Volume (PSV).
